newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ANGLO GIVES GO-AHEAD TO NAMAKWA 2ND PHASE.
newsitem.headline: ANGLO GIVES GO-AHEAD TO NAMAKWA 2ND PHASE.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said on Wednesday it would proceed with Phase 2 of the Namakwa Sands project at a cost of 1.2 billion rand, bringing the total capital investment in the project to 2.1 billion rand.
Phase 2 involves the construction of a second ilmenite smelting furnace at Saldanha for production of titanium dioxide slag and pig iron.
This will increase production of slag to about 235,000 tonnes a year from 97,000. Production of pig iron will increase to 130,000 tonnes from 56,000.
Anglo said in a statement that the mining and mineral processing facilities in the Vredendal/Lutzville area will expand to provide the additional ilmenite for the second furnace.
This will lead to a significant increase in production of zircon to about 140,000 tonnes per year and 42,000 tonnes of rutile.
Anglo said the increased production will be exported and export earnings will increase to approximately 750 million rand a year.
The second phase of the project was included in the original environmental impact assessment carried out in 1992.
The expansion will create an additional 260 jobs, Anglo said.
The Namakwa Sands heavy minerals project was funded by equity capital from Anglo (80 percent) and De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd .
The project also received a 370 million rand from the state's Industrial Development Corporation.
Anglo said the available in situ reserves were in excess of 500 million tonnes which would be sufficient to sustain operations for more than 35 years.
